question.text: Mrs. Kaur has accumulated Rs. 30 lakh in an equity mutual fund and wants a regular monthly income of Rs. 25,000 from it. Which facility should she use?

explanation.text: The Logic: NISM-Series-X-A (pp.220-221) describes SWP as a facility that enables recurring redemptions from a scheme over a period of time at the applicable NAV, suitable for an investor seeking a regular payout. Mrs. Kaur can set up monthly redemptions of Rs. 25,000 while the remaining corpus continues to be invested. The Trap: STP transfers units between schemes of the same fund rather than paying out to the investor, and DTP routes dividends to another scheme — neither delivers regular cash to the unit holder. Note: Tax-treatment comparisons between SWP and IDCW are not in the checked SWP/STP/DTP pages and should be cited from a separate tax source before being asserted.
